title: Booking rack: Total receipt
topics: Greedy choices, dynamic programming and backtracking
summary: Greedy interval selection. Add all numbers in the result list.
descriptionMd:
Your task
Build a result list using Step 1. Then use that list to find the answer in Step 2.

Inputs
drawers is a list of bookings. Each row is [start, end]. k is included in the function call, but this task does not use it. You can ignore it.

Step 1: Build the result list
Each booking is [start, end]. It uses time from start up to, but not including, end. Sort bookings by end time, from earliest to latest. For matching end times, put the earlier start first. Accept the first booking. Then accept a booking only if it starts at or after the end of the last one accepted. Record the length, end - start, of each accepted booking. Keep acceptance order. Negative times are allowed. With no bookings, the result list is empty.

Step 2: Return the answer
Add all numbers in the result list. Return the total. An empty list has a total of 0.

Write your function
Complete bookingRackTotalReceipt(drawers, k). Return the answer from Step 2. Do not print it or read keyboard input. In examples, positions (indexes) start at 0 unless a rule says otherwise.

Each card first builds this result list, then asks for a different answer. Start with the first card. The last card also uses position numbers that start at 1.
constraints: k is a whole number from 1 to 8. Answers fit in a signed 32-bit integer: -2,147,483,648 through 2,147,483,647.
Input numbers have no decimal part. They range from -1,000,000 to 1,000,000. Follow any extra input rules in Step 1.
Efficiency goal: time O(n log n); extra memory, including the result list, O(n). n is the input length. These labels describe how work and memory grow with the input.
